topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Biological origins of cancer and susceptibility to mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can produce cancer through clonal evolution in a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the evidence for their importance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence about environmental exposures informs the debate over whether cancer is preventable or unavoidable.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between pathogens and cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: How environmental carcinogens damage DNA
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular processes through which environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-producing initiation from the promotion of tumour growth and explain why both can be necessary for cancer development.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the cellular context of exposure affects carcinogenesis and consolidate that point within the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methods and limitations of establishing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence linking exposures to cancer is obtained and why the available methods cannot fully reproduce or resolve human carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing exposure decisions as a balance of risks and benefits.
